note: lem prune: the developer's own state.keep_days over the team's in both orders (test_the_days_are_the_developers_own_over_the_teams_and_say_where_they_come_from), from a task's worktree, with the file it came from in `from`; the command is `lem prune`, no longer `lem project prune`

the small record is task.json (journal folded, citations cleared), sessions.jsonl, session-acts.jsonl, ask.txt, task.md, parked.json and the locks; the ticket and the resume are fields of the record; old folders, links, an unread record, a failed removal and the dry run each have their case in test_retention.py and test_prune.py

an old ended task's journal becomes one Summary entry of its own record (no shared event log); task.json stays, so a new task cannot take its name and a task queued after it still starts (queue.turn reads its status)
The old question expires. An unrelated dated folder stays.
the command is `lem prune [--dry-run] [--days N]` (surfaces.md A); a failed removal is a refusal that names it (exit 1)
a moved-base refusal keeps the owner's merge, and a safe read lets the board server carry it out

no separate look and no kept model of the sessions: each duty that reads them asks the terminal at its tick, an unreadable list is the board's problem; the board's views read the sessions themselves (board-views)
the server says whether the forge queued or completed the merge; test_bookkeeping_follows_a_server_merge_before_the_next_forge_poll proves the completed merge's line

a Summary entry of the task's journal (records/journal/task.py), with the run of statuses, the last state, the first and last moments, the entries folded, the pull request, green and reasons, the plan talk and the totals of spans and waits; the task's own fields stay on the task
the server merges the new tip after a real new round and merge read; the proposal's dependency for carry is in notes/land-propose.md
the merge runs in this process (app/landing/merge.py); its refusal's why and fix are the line the board shows, in place of land.py's standard error
as the merge lock's: the step lock's refusal, with its why and fix, is the line the board shows
the duties call the app in this process and read each task's newest session from Lem's acts on it; no `lem session list` output is parsed
which read answers Lem's refusal for the moved base is land-merge's (app/landing/mergeread.py clears the refusal); the duty merges only once the record says so
the read that answers the refusal is land-merge's rule; the duty follows the record
the real landing makes and clears the refusal and the board server merges on the owner's word
the line names the journal entries folded, in the place of the log's events
the release rule applies without a saved hold, and cleanup still gets its wake
the turn is an act in session-acts.jsonl, and the guard takes the `worked` step (main held it back one release; notes/sessions.md)
the server keeps no model of the sessions: each tick reads the session's signs where a duty needs them, and the board's views read a turn that runs themselves (board-views)

a task is dated by its record (Task.since and its journal), so no log can disagree with it; a record that does not read is skipped and named (test_a_link_is_never_followed_and_a_record_that_does_not_read_keeps_every_file)
no shared log is rewritten: retention rechecks the task revision and session activity together under the task lock (test_a_cleanup_wake_after_classification_keeps_the_whole_task)
the record's lock and its revision (store/tasks.py, core's) hold every write of a record; no event log is appended to
a write between the fold's read and its write is refused by the revision, and the fold waits for the next run
each task has its own record, so the fold of one touches no other's; the old task's journal is one Summary (test_a_run_past_the_cutoff_leaves_an_old_ended_task_its_small_record_only)
the investigation stays on the task, with its report's path cleared
the night and the spans stay on the task; the summary keeps the totals (test_the_summary_keeps_the_statuses_the_last_state_the_pull_request_and_the_totals)
no command writes a journal entry by its kind, so none can write a summary; retention's fold is its one writer (store/retention/rules.folded_into)
